source_blocks.heading: ANNEX A - Age Verification Profile
source_blocks.excerpt: (normative)

source_blocks.heading: A.1. Introduction
source_blocks.excerpt:
This document defines a set of requirements for the existing specifications to
enable interoperability among Attestation Providers (APs), Age Verification App Instances (AVIs)
and Relying Parties (RPs) where a substantial level of security and privacy is required.
This document is an interoperability profile that can be used by implementations
in various contexts, be it a certain industry or a certain regulatory environment.

source_blocks.heading: A.1. Introduction
source_blocks.excerpt:
This profile is part of the EU Age Verification technical specifications. It builds
on existing specifications commonly used for credential issuance and verification
and defines a set of features to be implemented in the context of age verification

source_blocks.heading: A.1. Introduction
source_blocks.excerpt:
This document outlines a profile for the age verification target architecture,
serving as a conceptual framework rather than a comprehensive specification of all
features and requirements. At the current stage of development, not all functionalities
described herein have been implemented in the Age Verification Solution Toolbox.
Furthermore, certain features are also absent in the present development state of
the EUDI Wallet libraries. These functionalities will be developed and integrated
incrementally over the course of the project.

source_blocks.heading: A.1. Introduction
source_blocks.excerpt:
The profile uses OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance [OID4VCI] for issuance
of Proof of Age attestations. Furthermore, for the presentation of Proof of Age
attestations, the profile uses the W3C Digital Credentials API [W3C Digital Credentials API] as specified in
\[ISO/IEC 18013-7\], Annex C, as well as OpenID for Verifiable Presentations [OID4VP]
as a fallback mechanism. The attestation format used is ISO mDoc [ISO18013-5].

source_blocks.heading: A.1. Introduction
source_blocks.excerpt:
A full list of the open standards used in this profile can be found in Overview of
the Open Standards Requirements.

source_blocks.heading: Target audience/Usage
source_blocks.excerpt:
The intended audience for this document comprises Member States and designated
organizations that seek to implement an age verification solution. This profile,
the referenced technical standards and accompanying guidelines are designed to
support governmental authorities as well as commissioned organizations in the
development, integration, and deployment of compliant age verification systems
within their respective jurisdictions or operational domains. This approach ensures
that both public sector bodies and their authorized private sector partners are
equipped to realize and maintain robust, privacy-preserving age verification in
alignment with European regulatory requirements, age verification digital services
requirements, and digital identity initiatives.

source_blocks.heading: A.2. Terminology
source_blocks.excerpt:
This specification uses the terms
Attestation Providers (APs), Age Verification App Instances (AVIs), Relying Parties (RPs), Proof of Age attestation, and AVS Unit Attestation (AVSUA) as defined in [Operational, Security, Product, and Architecture Specifications](../../../docs/architecture-and-technical-specifications.md).

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt:
The primary focus of this document is on online services, with the intention that
age verification should be conducted digitally in online environments. The solution
is specifically designed to enable users to prove their age when accessing online
content, products, or services that are subject to age restrictions. This approach
addresses the increasing need for robust online age verification mechanisms,
ensuring that age-restricted content is accessed only by individuals who meet
the required legal age, and supporting compliance with relevant regulatory
requirements for online platforms.

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: The following aspects are in scope of this interoperability profile:

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Profile of OpenID4VCI to issue ISO mDoc Proof of Age attestations

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Profile of OpenID4VP to present ISO mDoc Proof of Age attestation

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Crypto Suites

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Data model examples

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: The following assumptions are made:

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - The APs and RPs cannot pre-discover Age Verification App’s capability

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - The AP is talking to the AVI supporting the features defined in this profile (via AVI invocation mechanism)

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Support for mDoc only as the Proof of Age attestation format

source_blocks.heading: A.3. Scope
source_blocks.excerpt:
- No personal data, especially no information from personal identification documents
such as national ID card, is stored within an AVI. Only the Proof of Age attestation,
specifically indicating "older than 18", is utilized for age verification purposes

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: The following items are out of scope for the current version of this document, but might be added in future versions:

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Support for Level of Assurance (LoA) "high".

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Proof of Age attestation re-issuance (using refresh tokens) and revocation.

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - RP registration and trusted lists of RPs.

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Trusted lists of Age Verification App providers under the envisaged EU Age Verification Scheme (the interim publication of provider certificates by the Commission is described in the Operational, Security, Product, and Architecture Specifications, Section 4.2).

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Proof of Age attestation presentation using proximity.

source_blocks.heading: Out of Scope
source_blocks.excerpt: - Profile of OpenID4VCI to issue ISO mDoc [ISO.18013-5] is defined in ISO 23220-3.

source_blocks.heading: Standards Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: This specification enables interoperable implementations of the following flows:

source_blocks.heading: Standards Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - Issuance of ISO mDoc Proof of Age attestation using OpenID4VCI

source_blocks.heading: Standards Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt:
- Presentation of ISO mDoc Proof of Age attestation using OpenID4VP
Implementations of this specification do not have to implement all of the flows listed above.
A parameter that is listed as optional to be implemented in a specification that is
being profiled (i.e., OpenID4VCI, OpenID4VP and ISO mDoc) remains optional unless it is stated otherwise in this specification.

source_blocks.heading: A.4 Proof of Age attestation Data Model
source_blocks.excerpt:
The data model for the Proof of Age attestation is defined as a profile of
the attribute schema specified in \[ISO/IEC 18013-5\]
and \[ISO/IEC 23220-2\]. A Proof of Age attestation SHALL comply with this data model.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.1 Document type
source_blocks.excerpt: The document type for Proof of Age attestation SHALL be `eu.europa.ec.av.1`.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt:
The Proof of Age attestation attribute set SHALL be composed of attributes defined in the following
Table. All attributes belong to namespace `eu.europa.ec.av.1`

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: | Identifier | Meaning | Presence in issuance | Presence in verification | Encoding format |

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: | age\_over\_18 | This attribute is present in all Proof of Age attestations and indicates whether the user is above 18\. | Mandatory | Conditional mandatory (either age\_over\_18 or one of age\_over\_NN attributes SHALL be requested) | bool |

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: | age\_over\_NN | Confirming whether the Proof of Age attestation user is currently over NN years of age. Multiple entries MAY be provided as separate attributes. | Optional | Conditional mandatory (either age\_over\_18 or one of age\_over\_NN attributes SHALL be requested)  | bool |

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: A Proof of Age Attestation SHALL NOT include any other attribute.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: **Note on Age Attribute Scope**

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt:
While the technical architecture and data model (based on \[ISO/IEC 18013-5\]
and \[ISO/IEC 23220-2\]) inherently support the age\_over\_NN attribute schema
for arbitrary age thresholds (e.g., age\_over\_14, age\_over\_65), this
specification explicitly focuses on age\_over\_18 to address the most common
regulatory requirement for age-restricted online services in the EU.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: Extending the solution to additional age thresholds would require:

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: 1. Validation of enrolment methods for the target age group.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt: 2. Alignment with jurisdictional legal frameworks governing the specific age-based restrictions.

source_blocks.heading: A.4.2 Attribute set
source_blocks.excerpt:
Section 7.2.5 \[ISO/IEC 18013-5\] of specification 'Age attestation: nearest “true”
attestation above request' may be considered in implementations making use of
the optional age_over_NN attribute.

source_blocks.heading: A.5. Proof of Age Attestation Issuance
source_blocks.excerpt:
Issuance of Proof of Age attestations SHOULD follow the issuance framework
defined for the EUDI Wallet in the [EUDI Wallet ARF](https://eu-digital-identity-wallet.github.io/eudi-doc-architecture-and-reference-framework/),
which is based on OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance.

source_blocks.heading: A.5. Proof of Age Attestation Issuance
source_blocks.excerpt:
An Attestation Provider and an Age Verification App Provider MAY instead agree on an internal
issuance interface (for example, where both roles are performed by the same or
affiliated entities), provided that it achieves equivalent assurance, in
particular regarding the verification of the legitimacy of the requesting AVI
(see AVS Unit Attestation below).

source_blocks.heading: Credential Offer
source_blocks.excerpt: - As a way to invoke the AVI, at least a custom URL scheme av-vci:// MUST be supported.

source_blocks.heading: AVS Unit Attestation
source_blocks.excerpt:
When following the EUDI Wallet issuance framework, the AVI SHOULD present an AVS Unit
Attestation (AVSUA) to the AP during issuance. The AVSUA comprises an Age Verification App
Instance Attestation (AVIA), attesting to the integrity of the AVI, and a Key Attestation
(KA), attesting to the security of the keys the AVI uses in the issuance flow. Both are
issued and signed by the provider of the Age Verification solution, which performs for the
AVI the role that [TS3] assigns to the Wallet Provider.

source_blocks.heading: AVS Unit Attestation
source_blocks.excerpt:
The AVSUA is the Age Verification instantiation of the Wallet Unit Attestation mechanism
specified in [TS3]: the AVIA corresponds to the Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) and the KA
to the Key Attestation of that specification. Implementations MAY reuse Wallet Unit
Attestation implementations for this purpose. The [ARF] provides the wider context.

source_blocks.heading: AVS Unit Attestation
source_blocks.excerpt:
Note (informative): on the trust anchor for AVSUA validation and its evolution under the
envisaged EU Age Verification Scheme, see Section 3.4.4 of the Operational, Security,
Product, and Architecture Specifications.

source_blocks.heading: A.6. Proof of Age attestation presentation
source_blocks.excerpt: Presentation involves two choices: the presentation mechanism and the transport. The two are not independent, since the Zero-Knowledge Proof mechanism is available only over the W3C Digital Credentials API transport.

source_blocks.heading: A.6. Proof of Age attestation presentation
source_blocks.excerpt: - **Presentation mechanism.** The preferred mechanism is a Zero-Knowledge Proof defined in Section A.8. A plain ISO mDoc presentation SHALL be used as the fallback where, and only where, either (a) the User's device does not support Zero-Knowledge Proof generation, or (b) the OpenID for Verifiable Presentations transport is used.

source_blocks.heading: A.6. Proof of Age attestation presentation
source_blocks.excerpt: - **Transport.** The default transport is the W3C Digital Credentials API. OpenID for Verifiable Presentations is used as a transport fallback when the Digital Credentials API is not available.

source_blocks.heading: W3C Digital Credentials API
source_blocks.excerpt:
Presentation as a Zero-Knowledge Proof over the W3C Digital Credentials API SHALL follow Section A.8, which specifies the normative request and response format by reference; a non-normative example is provided in Section A.11 ("W3C Digital Credentials API with ZKP"). The plain ISO mDoc presentation described below is the fallback mechanism, used under the conditions set out at the beginning of this section.
The W3C Digital Credentials API is used as specified in \[ISO/IEC 18013-7\], Annex C.

source_blocks.heading: Request
source_blocks.excerpt:
The Relying Party builds a request which consists of two parts: `encryptionInfo`
and `deviceRequest`.

source_blocks.heading: Request
source_blocks.excerpt:
**Encryption info**
`encryptionInfo` is the base64-url without padding encoding of the cbor
encoded `EncryptionInfo` object defined below

source_blocks.heading: Request
Request
source_blocks.excerpt:
**Device Request**
`deviceRequest` is the base64-url without padding encoding of the cbor encoded
`DeviceRequest` defined in \[ISO/IEC 18013-5\] §8.3.2.1.2.1

source_blocks.heading: Response
source_blocks.excerpt:
The response is the base64-url without padding encoding of the cbor
encoded `EncryptedResponse` object defined below:

source_blocks.heading: Response
Response
source_blocks.excerpt:
`enc` is the public key used for the generation of the ciphertext, which is used
in the decryption process, and `cipherText` is the encrypted response, which is
a `DeviceResponse`, defined in Section 8.3.2.1.2.3 of ISO/IEC 18013-5, encrypted
using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) defined in RFC 9180.

source_blocks.heading: Reader Authentication
source_blocks.excerpt: Reader authentication is not required and therefore is out of scope of this profile

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt:
OpenID for Verifiable Presentations is used as a transport fallback when W3C
Digital Credentials API is not available. Zero-Knowledge Proofs are not supported over OpenID for Verifiable Presentations in this version of the profile, since no standardized DCQL query for requesting Zero-Knowledge Proof is available. This transport is for ISO mDoc format attestations only. This transport will be revisited once the relevan standardisation work has concluded.

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - As a way to invoke the Age Verification App, at least a custom URL scheme av:// MUST be supported.

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - Response type MUST be `vp_token`

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - `response_mode` MUST be `direct_post`

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - RP MUST send the request as URL-encoded query parameters. The `request` and `request_uri` parameters MUST NOT be used (i.e., support for JAR is not required)

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - The client identifier scheme MUST be `redirect_uri` followed by the `response_uri`

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - A request MUST specify the nonce parameter

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - The DCQL query and response as defined in Section 6 of [OID4VP] MUST be used

source_blocks.heading: OpenID for Verifiable Presentations profile Requirements
source_blocks.excerpt: - The `state` parameter as defined in Section 4.1.1 of [OID4VP] is optional

source_blocks.heading: Client Authentication
source_blocks.excerpt: Client authentication is not required and is therefore out of scope of this profile.

source_blocks.heading: A.7. Crypto Suites
source_blocks.excerpt:
All entities MUST support P-256 (secp256r1) as a key type with ES256 JWT algorithm for signing and signature validation
whenever this profile requires to do so.
SHA256 MUST be supported by all the entities as the hash algorithm to generate and validate the digests in the MDOC VC.
Note: When using this profile with other cryptosuites, it is recommended to be explicit about which entity is required
to support which curve for signing and/or signature validation.

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt:
Where the User's device provides the necessary platform support, the AVI SHALL support the generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs using the solution detailed in: *"Matteo Frigo and abhi shelat, Anonymous credentials from ECDSA,
IACR Communications in Cryptology, vol. 3, no. 1, 2026, available at [https://doi.org/10.62056/a3qjmpgxq](https://doi.org/10.62056/a3qjmpgxq)"* [Fri2024].
An open-source implementation of this solution has been released [here](https://github.com/google/longfellow-zk). A Zero-Knowledge Proof is the preferred mechanism for presenting a Proof of Age attestation. It is requested and returned over the W3C Digital Credentials API.

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: For this version of the profile, the only Zero-Knowledge Proof system in scope is the system identified by `longfellow-libzk-v1`, as defined in [Fri2024] and specified in [draft-google-cfrg-libzk](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-google-cfrg-libzk/), using the circuit and parameters identified by the ZkSystemSpec parameters (`circuit_hash`, `version`, `num_attributes`, `block_enc_hash`, `block_enc_sig`) as defined in ISO/IEC DIS 18013-5 (Second Edition), Section 10.2.7. An implementation SHALL use that system. Support for any other Zero-Knowledge Proof system does not constitute conformance with this profile. The system identifier is versioned, and future versions of this profile may add or replace the systems in scope. The set of circuits accepted for the purposes of this profile, identified by their circuit hashes, is published and maintained by the scheme owner separately from this document.

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: The request and response structure of a Zero-Knowledge Proof presentation SHALL follow the ZkSystemSpec mechanism defined in ISO/IEC 18013-5 (Second Edition), Section 10.2.7, transported over the W3C Digital Credentials API as specified in ISO/IEC 18013-7, Annex C. The proof format SHALL follow [draft-google-cfrg-libzk]; a non-normative example is provided in Section A.11 ("W3C Digital Credentials API with ZKP").

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: Such a proof SHALL demonstrate that:

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - The Proof of Age attestation includes a signature that can be verified using the public key of the AP

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - The Proof of Age attestation includes the requested attribute and its value is true

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt:
- The AVI can generate a signature of the nonce that is verifiable using the
public key included in the Proof of attestation

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - The Proof of Age attestation is within its validity period

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: Verification requirements:

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - An RP SHALL be able to verify these Zero-Knowledge Proofs.

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - An RP SHALL verify that the Zero-Knowledge Proof was generated using an accepted circuit, by verifying the circuit hash against the set of circuits accepted for the purposes of this profile, before verifying the proof. An RP SHALL reject a presentation generated using a circuit that is not among the accepted circuits.

source_blocks.heading: A.8. Zero-Knowledge Proofs
source_blocks.excerpt: - Where the User's device does not support Zero-Knowledge Proof generation, the AVI SHALL fall back to the plain ISO mDoc presentation defined in Section A.6. The RP SHALL be able to verify both a Zero-Knowledge Proof presentation and the plain ISO mDoc fallback presentation.

source_blocks.heading: A.9. Security Considerations
source_blocks.excerpt: The security considerations in [OID4VCI] and [OID4VP] apply when compatible with Level of Assurance substantial only.

source_blocks.heading: A.9. Security Considerations
source_blocks.excerpt: Because Relying Parties cannot pre-discover the capabilities of an Age Verification App Instance, a Relying Party cannot distinguish a User device that lacks Zero-Knowledge Proof support from a presentation that has been downgraded to the fallback mechanism. A Relying Party SHALL NOT reject a presentation solely on the ground that it uses the plain ISO mDoc fallback mechanism. Note that the plain ISO mDoc presentation does not provide the unlinkability properties of the Zero-Knowledge Proof mechanism (see Annex B); the residual linkability risk is mitigated by the batch issuance and single-use requirements of the main specification.

tests.asserts: Checks the emitted CBOR EncryptionInfo array discriminator, nonce key presence and bare COSE_Key map shape.
tests.limits: Does not assert base64url padding, complete ISO conformance, plain mdoc fallback, or all COSE_Key members.

tests.asserts: Builds an AV-doctype DeviceRequest, decodes selected request and ZK system fields and compares its bytes with the committed request vector.
tests.limits: No explicit assertion of docType, namespace or age predicate; not a plain mdoc fallback test or a proof that the profile parameter tuple and scheme-owner circuits are accepted.

tests.asserts: Checks nonce length, local HPKE seal/open round trip with a transcript and rejection of a flipped ciphertext bit.
tests.limits: Uses arbitrary plaintext, not a DeviceResponse, and does not assert EncryptedResponse wrapper or complete base64url encoding.

tests.asserts: Checks generated JWK EC/P-256 labels, 32-byte x coordinate and 32-byte thumbprint.
tests.limits: Local verifier key generation only; not every entity or all signing and validation operations.

tests.asserts: Signs a compact JWS and verifies that its payload round trips using the public key.
tests.limits: Local P-256/ES256 primitive only; no AVI/AP interoperability or entire-entity algorithm coverage.

tests.asserts: A local registry containing only deadbeef refuses the computed circuit for parameters (7,1).
tests.limits: Local allowlist check only. The scheme-owner accepted set and its publication/authority are [UNVERIFIED]; not AV circuit acceptance evidence.
tests.requires: Go/cgo and Rust staticlib from make deps

tests.asserts: Asserts AV docType/namespace/age predicate in the copied minted document and local requests; checks all five nested tuple fields and compares independent CBOR/JSON fixtures with runtime DeviceRequest and ZkAgeQuery.
tests.limits: Only fixture identities and request construction are covered. The copied proof binds OpenID4VPHandover; no new proof, issuance enforcement, DC API proof verification or full attribute allowlist is established.

tests.asserts: Accepts the positive local longfellow-libzk-v1 version-7 AV tuple with the actual verifier allowlist; rejects each of five missing and tampered parameters and an unknown system.
tests.limits: Exercises local DCQL allowlist validation with the profile parameter names. Existing carrier policy also accepts the legacy org.iso.mdoc.zk alias; this compatibility exception does not establish AV system exclusivity. The unofficial OpenID4VP ZK carrier is not AV transport conformance. The scheme-owner accepted set/publication/authority and external standards editions remain [UNVERIFIED].

tests.asserts: Independently compares all 32 A.11 fenced literal bodies and ten binary decodes; checks DC API request/encrypted-response containers, AV doctype and all five version-6 example parameters; refuses those external tuples against the local version-7 allowlist.
tests.limits: Non-normative external container examples only. Ciphertexts are retained without decryption, diagnostics are literal text and no external proof is verified. Full inherited ISO/proof schemas, DC API end-to-end operation and scheme acceptance remain unevidenced.

tests.asserts: Calls NewHPKEKeyPair and DeviceRequest for the AV doctype and confirms both returned request components are populated.
tests.limits: Only primitive component construction is covered; no complete outer request, wire transport, device support or standards-complete request schema is established.

tests.asserts: Checks NewHPKEKeyPair encryptionInfo is unpadded base64url and decodes to nonempty encoded bytes.
tests.limits: Does not validate every nested CBOR/COSE field or complete ISO/DC API behavior.

tests.asserts: Checks BuildDCAPIEnvelope output round trips through unpadded base64url encoding.
tests.limits: Uses a minimal envelope; does not establish a complete DeviceResponse or inherited wire schema.

tests.asserts: Checks ParseEnvelope extracts enc and cipherText and rejects malformed discriminator, field type, truncation and missing-field cases.
tests.limits: Selected parser structure only; no complete CDDL validation or base64url endpoint behavior.

tests.asserts: Inspects presenter.request and asserts response_type is vp_token.
tests.limits: Only local request-object construction; no externally served AV fallback interoperability.

tests.asserts: Inspects presenter.request against the AV profile direct_post requirement.
tests.limits: Known candidate mismatch is reported as FAIL; no production policy is changed.

tests.asserts: Inspects handleNew response wallet URI for request_uri transport against AV URL-query requirements.
tests.limits: Known candidate mismatch is reported as FAIL; complete URI/query semantics are not implemented.

tests.asserts: Checks request client_id follows redirect_uri identification and matches response_uri.
tests.limits: Known candidate mismatch is reported as FAIL; certificate identity and endpoint trust are outside scope.

tests.asserts: Asserts the generated presentation request contains a nonce.
tests.limits: Local session request only; no independent wallet echo/binding property is asserted.

tests.asserts: Validates the candidate DCQL request and checks the requested fallback format is mso_mdoc.
tests.limits: Known candidate mismatch is reported as FAIL; no full OpenID4VP response conformance.

tests.asserts: Checks emitted state retains the session identifier.
tests.limits: State is optional in the profile; this checks only candidate behavior when emitted.

enable interoperability among Attestation Providers (APs), Age Verification App Instances (AVIs)

in various contexts, be it a certain industry or a certain regulatory environment.

clauses.excerpt:
The primary focus of this document is on online services, with the intention that
age verification should be conducted digitally in online environments. The solution
is specifically designed to enable users to prove their age when accessing online
content, products, or services that are subject to age restrictions. This approach
addresses the increasing need for robust online age verification mechanisms,
ensuring that age-restricted content is accessed only by individuals who meet
the required legal age, and supporting compliance with relevant regulatory
requirements for online platforms.

When following the EUDI Wallet issuance framework, the AVI SHOULD present an AVS Unit
Attestation (AVSUA) to the AP during issuance. The AVSUA comprises an Age Verification App
Instance Attestation (AVIA), attesting to the integrity of the AVI, and a Key Attestation
(KA), attesting to the security of the keys the AVI uses in the issuance flow. Both are
issued and signed by the provider of the Age Verification solution, which performs for the
AVI the role that [TS3] assigns to the Wallet Provider.

Attestation implementations for this purpose. The [ARF] provides the wider context.

clauses.excerpt:
Where the User's device provides the necessary platform support, the AVI SHALL support the generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs using the solution detailed in: *"Matteo Frigo and abhi shelat, Anonymous credentials from ECDSA,
IACR Communications in Cryptology, vol. 3, no. 1, 2026, available at [https://doi.org/10.62056/a3qjmpgxq](https://doi.org/10.62056/a3qjmpgxq)"* [Fri2024].
An open-source implementation of this solution has been released [here](https://github.com/google/longfellow-zk). A Zero-Knowledge Proof is the preferred mechanism for presenting a Proof of Age attestation. It is requested and returned over the W3C Digital Credentials API.

clauses.excerpt: For this version of the profile, the only Zero-Knowledge Proof system in scope is the system identified by `longfellow-libzk-v1`, as defined in [Fri2024] and specified in [draft-google-cfrg-libzk](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-google-cfrg-libzk/), using the circuit and parameters identified by the ZkSystemSpec parameters (`circuit_hash`, `version`, `num_attributes`, `block_enc_hash`, `block_enc_sig`) as defined in ISO/IEC DIS 18013-5 (Second Edition), Section 10.2.7. An implementation SHALL use that system. Support for any other Zero-Knowledge Proof system does not constitute conformance with this profile. The system identifier is versioned, and future versions of this profile may add or replace the systems in scope. The set of circuits accepted for the purposes of this profile, identified by their circuit hashes, is published and maintained by the scheme owner separately from this document.

The proof format SHALL follow [draft-google-cfrg-libzk]; a non-normative example is provided in Section A.11 ("W3C Digital Credentials API with ZKP").

clauses.out_of_scope_for_v1: out of scope for v1: Inherited OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP security considerations conditional on substantial assurance are retained without expanding unverified external requirements.

clauses.excerpt: Because Relying Parties cannot pre-discover the capabilities of an Age Verification App Instance, a Relying Party cannot distinguish a User device that lacks Zero-Knowledge Proof support from a presentation that has been downgraded to the fallback mechanism.
clauses.out_of_scope_for_v1: out of scope for v1: No AV plain mdoc fallback acceptance/non-rejection test; the repository ZK-only verifier does not prove this. Main-spec batch issuance/single-use linkability mitigations are not independently verified here.

clauses.excerpt: A Relying Party SHALL NOT reject a presentation solely on the ground that it uses the plain ISO mDoc fallback mechanism.
clauses.out_of_scope_for_v1: out of scope for v1: No AV plain mdoc fallback acceptance/non-rejection test; the repository ZK-only verifier does not prove this. Main-spec batch issuance/single-use linkability mitigations are not independently verified here.

clauses.excerpt: Note that the plain ISO mDoc presentation does not provide the unlinkability properties of the Zero-Knowledge Proof mechanism (see Annex B); the residual linkability risk is mitigated by the batch issuance and single-use requirements of the main specification.
